question: Which type of memory is non-volatile and is used to store essential system instructions in a computer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a type of non-volatile memory used to store essential system instructions that remain intact even when the computer is powered off.
 
• It contains firmware, which is permanently written by the manufacturer and cannot be modified by the user under normal conditions.
 
• ROM is crucial for the booting process as it stores the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or UEFI firmware instructions.
 
• Unlike RAM, the data in ROM is persistent and not lost when the system is shut down, making it ideal for storing critical instructions.
 
• Examples of ROM include **EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM)** and **EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM)**, which are more flexible variations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**

 
 
• RAM is a volatile memory type used for temporary data storage while a program is running.
 
• It provides faster read and write speeds compared to ROM but loses all data when the computer is turned off.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are high-speed storage locations within the CPU used to store temporary data and instructions.
 
• They are much smaller in size but faster compared to both RAM and ROM.
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• Cache memory is a small-sized type of volatile memory located close to the CPU to store frequently accessed data and instructions.
 
• It significantly enhances the processing speed by reducing the time required to access data from the main memory.
 
 
 
• **Types of ROM:**
 
 
• **Masked ROM:** Pre-programmed at the time of manufacturing.
 
• **PROM:** Programmable Read-Only Memory that can be written once.
 
• **EPROM:** Can be erased using ultraviolet light and reprogrammed.
 
• **EEPROM:** Can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.
